intent: vendor preset "Blizzard" (Nature) — validate against its thumbnail

iterations.critique: The render clearly reads as a dense white blizzard on black, with strong depth layering and convincing forward motion between t1 and t4. The t1 frame has a good mix of fine snow and nearer flakes. By t4, however, several foreground particles become excessively large, soft, and blown-out—especially along the upper-right and lower-right—making the result feel more like fast camera-flight debris than consistently scaled snowfall. The depth motion is strong but slightly too aggressive over the short frame interval.

The render strongly reads as a dense white blizzard on black, with convincing multilayered snow density and a good fine-particle field at t1. Motion/depth progression is still too aggressive by t4: numerous foreground flakes have expanded into large, soft, overbright discs, especially near the upper-left, upper-right, and lower-right edges. This makes the effect feel like particles rapidly flying into the camera rather than the more consistently scaled snowfall implied by the Blizzard preset thumbnail.

The render now reads convincingly as a dense white blizzard with a strong field of fine flakes, black-background contrast, and far more consistent particle sizing than prior iterations. The oversized blown-out foreground discs are largely resolved. Between t1 and t4, however, the field still gains depth and apparent density a little too quickly, with a handful of noticeably larger near flakes at the edges. It remains slightly more like forward flight through particles than the steadier snowfall suggested by the preset thumbnail.
